paragraphs.text: Intermediate junctional epidermolysis bullosa-5A (JEB5A) is an autosomal recessive blistering disorder caused by mutation in the gene for integrin beta-4 (ITGB4). Skin involvement is milder than in the lethal form of epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia, and affected patients survive beyond infancy. Pyloric atresia may be present (Mellerio et al., 1998) or absent (Inoue et al., 2000; Jonkman et al., 2002). Reported features include acral blistering, nail dystrophy and enamel hypoplasia (Jonkman et al., 2002).

paragraphs.text: Jonkman et al. (2002) reported a 49-year-old woman who had had mild blistering of the hands and feet since birth, nail dystrophy with onychogryposis, and enamel hypoplasia. She had no alopecia and no history of pyloric atresia. Electron microscopy and antigen mapping of a skin blister showed an intraepidermal split, located low in the basal keratinocytes through the attachment plaque of the hemidesmosome. The authors described the phenotype as having predominant features of epidermolysis bullosa simplex.

paragraphs.text: In their 49-year-old patient, Jonkman et al. (2002) found a novel heterozygous 2-bp deletion (4733delCT) in the ITGB4 gene. The deletion caused in-frame skipping of exon 36, which was predicted to remove 50 amino acids (residues 1450-1499) within the third fibronectin type III repeat of the beta-4 cytoplasmic domain. Immunoblot analysis showed a beta-4 polypeptide 5 kDa shorter than normal. Because no full-size protein was detected in vitro and the 450-11A epitope was absent in vivo, the authors expected the patient to also be heterozygous for a null allele.
